papers.title: Target-controlled infusion of propofol induces rapid hypertriglyceridemia in healthy cats.
papers.authors: Arboit F, Mangini LT, Gasparotto JC, Griebeler LB, Oliveira JO, Vieira LS, Ohashi GS, Cadiñanos VDS, Paraguassú AO, Oberbeck EV
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To evaluate serum triglyceride concentrations during target-controlled infusion (TCI) of propofol in healthy cats undergoing elective orchiectomy and to investigate the relationship between cumulative propofol dose and triglyceride concentrations. METHODS: 8 healthy male cats were anesthetized using propofol administered via a TCI system targeting a plasma concentration of 7 µg/mL for 45 minutes. Blood samples were collected at baseline, after premedication, immediately after induction, and at 20 and 40 minutes of infusion for determination of serum triglyceride concentrations. RESULTS: Serum triglycerides increased significantly following propofol administration, with elevations detectable immediately after induction. Median concentrations were 41 mg/dL (range, 31 to 75) at baseline, 32 mg/dL (range, 20 to 99) after premedication, 128 mg/dL (range, 72 to 215) immediately after induction, 132 mg/dL (range, 106 to 227) at 20 minutes of infusion, and 143 mg/dL (range, 57 to 230) at 40 minutes of infusion. During anesthesia, 75% of the animals exceeded the reference interval for triglycerides. No significant correlation was observed between propofol cumulative doses and triglyceride concentrations. CONCLUSIONS: Target-controlled propofol infusion is associated with a rapid increase in serum triglyceride concentrations in cats even during short anesthetic procedures. CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Given the use of prolonged propofol infusions in veterinary anesthesia, these findings highlight the importance of considering potential changes in serum triglyceride concentrations, particularly in patients with underlying lipid or metabolic dysfunction.

papers.title: Doxorubicin-induced Cardiotoxicity in Dogs: A Narrative Review.
papers.authors: Sunpongsri S, Roos T, Gerhing R, Zandvliet M, Santarelli G
papers.abstract: Doxorubicin, an anthracycline widely used in both human and veterinary oncology, is highly effective against a variety of malignancies in dogs, including lymphomas, sarcomas and carcinomas. Despite its efficacy, doxorubicin exposure can be associated with cardiotoxicity, which may present acutely or chronically, potentially leading to severe cardiac arrhythmia and congestive heart failure. Mechanisms underlying cardiotoxicity are multifactorial, including oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, DNA damage via topoisomerase IIβ, inflammation and dysregulated cell death pathways such as apoptosis, pyroptosis and ferroptosis. In dogs, known risk factors include higher cumulative dose, breed predisposition to idiopathic dilated cardiomyopathy, and higher body weight. Cardiac biomarkers, electrocardiography, echocardiography and other advanced imaging techniques have been employed to detect cardiac changes that can be seen also in the absence of clinical signs. However, current evidence is predominantly derived from experimental and retrospective research, highlighting the need for large prospective clinical studies to strengthen recommendations for monitoring and prevention. A deeper understanding of doxorubicin-induced cardiotoxicity in dogs is needed to identify factors influencing individual susceptibility, clarify the progression from subclinical damage to clinical cardiac dysfunction, and guide future research. Emerging approaches, including advanced echocardiography, microRNAs, proteomic biomarkers and pharmacokinetic modelling, may help improve early detection and guide more individualised dosing to minimise toxicity.

papers.title: Urinary liver-type fatty acid-binding protein in cats with lower urinary tract disease.
papers.authors: Culha N, Acar A, Ulutas B, Dinler Ay C
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study was to evaluate urinary liver-type fatty acid-binding protein levels in both obstructive and non-obstructive feline lower urinary tract disease. In addition, urinary liver-type fatty acid-binding protein levels were investigated in cats experiencing short-term (<36 hours) and long-term (≥36 hours) urethral obstruction. MATERIALS AND METHODS: The study included 32 cats, classified into two main groups: cats with feline lower urinary tract disease (n = 24) and healthy controls (n = 8). The feline lower urinary tract disease group was subdivided into obstructive (n = 16) and non-obstructive (n = 8) forms. The obstructive group was further divided based on urethral obstruction duration into short-term (n = 8) and long-term (n = 8) sub-subgroups. Serum creatinine, blood urea nitrogen and potassium were measured in blood samples. Urinary liver-type fatty acid-binding protein and urinary creatinine concentrations were measured in urine supernatant samples. Urinary liver-type fatty acid-binding protein concentrations were indexed to urinary creatinine and expressed as the urinary liver-type fatty acid-binding protein/creatinine ratio. RESULTS: The mean urinary liver-type fatty acid-binding protein/creatinine values of cats with obstructive feline lower urinary tract disease were statistically higher than those in cats with non-obstructive feline lower urinary tract disease and healthy controls. The difference between the mean urinary liver-type fatty acid-binding protein/creatinine values of cats with long-term and short-term obstruction was not statistically significant. In addition, moderately positive correlations were calculated between urinary liver-type fatty acid-binding protein/creatinine and serum creatinine (r = .646; P < .001; 95% CI = 0.264 to 0.863) and between urinary liver-type fatty acid-binding protein/creatinine and blood urea nitrogen (r = .549; P < .01; 95% CI = 0.081 to 0.791) in the study population. CLINICAL SIGNIFICANCE: This study is the first to report urinary liver-type fatty acid-binding protein/creatinine in cats with feline lower urinary tract disease. The findings suggest that urinary liver-type fatty acid-binding protein/creatinine may serve as a potential biomarker for identifying post-renal acute kidney injury in cats with obstructive feline lower urinary tract disease, particularly in long-term obstructive cases.

papers.title: Peripheral pulmonary arterial stenosis due to lung tumor in a cat.
papers.authors: Morita T, Miyashita S, Miyamoto R, Fujiwara R
papers.abstract: A four-year-old castrated male American shorthair cat presented with lethargy, anorexia, and tachypnea. Echocardiography revealed a large mass compressing both branch pulmonary arteries. An increased peak systolic flow velocity in the left pulmonary artery (3.2 m/sec; estimated peak pressure gradient, 41 mmHg) was consistent with peripheral pulmonary arterial stenosis. Pulmonary hypertension was suspected based on echocardiographic findings. Computed tomography angiography demonstrated bilateral pulmonary artery stenosis by a pulmonary mass, and fine-needle biopsy cytology was consistent with lung carcinoma. Because of advanced disease with bilateral pulmonary artery involvement and suspected distant metastases, interventional treatment was not performed. This is the first report of acquired peripheral pulmonary arterial stenosis secondary to pulmonary carcinoma in a cat.

papers.title: Use of plasma chromogranin a epitopes vasostatin and catestatin as biomarkers for catecholamine-producing tumours in dogs.
papers.authors: Prabert J, Hanson J, Ishigaki K, Asano K, Höglund K, Stridsberg M, Höglund OV
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Differentiation of catecholamine-producing tumours from other adrenal tumours remains difficult. Chromogranin A (CgA) is a marker for catecholamine secretion in the body. An assay for quantification of the CgA epitopes vasostatin and catestatin has been validated for use in dogs but not yet evaluated in dogs with catecholamine-producing tumours. The aims were to evaluate the assays foranalysis of plasma concentrations of the CgA epitopes vasostatin and catestatin in dogs with adrenal tumours and to compare concentrations between catecholamine-producing tumours and adrenocortical tumours in dogs that were subjected to adrenalectomy. Twelve dogs with histopathologically confirmed catecholamine-secreting tumours (eleven pheochromocytomas (PCCs), one extra-adrenal sympathetic paraganglioma (PGL)) and twelve with adrenocortical tumours were included in the study. Plasma concentrations of the CgA epitopes vasostatin and catestatin were determined byradioimmunoassay (RIA), before adrenalectomy in 23 out of 24 dogs and after adrenalectomy in six of the dogs with catecholamine-secreting tumours (five PCC, one PGL). Tumour diagnosis was made by histopathology in all cases. RESULTS: Overall, median plasma concentration of the CgA epitopevasostatin in dogs with catecholamine-secreting tumours was 0.82 nmol/L (interquartile range (IQR) 0.52 to 1.60 nmol/L), which was significantly higher(Wilcoxon rank sum exact test, P= 0.0374) than the vasostatin concentration in adrenocortical tumours (median 0.50; IQR 0.34 to 0.59 nmol/L). A subsetof dogs (5/12) with catecholamine-secreting tumours had elevated plasma vasostatin concentrations preoperatively. After successful surgery, thepreoperatively elevated plasma vasostatin concentrations decreased numerically, however without reaching statistical significance. Catestatin concentrationdid not differ between tumour types. CONCLUSIONS: Elevated plasma concentration of the CgA epitope vasostatin showed potential as a biomarker for asubset of catecholamine-secreting tumours.

papers.title: A New Application of (64)CuCl(2) PET/CT: Imaging of Cats With Mammary Carcinoma.
papers.authors: Yang VA, Lunceford JM, Garrett C, Lattimer JC, Papageorgiou C, Smith CJ, Maitz CA, Bryan JN, Talbott JL, Lewis MR
papers.abstract: Feline mammary carcinoma (FMC) is an aggressive and highly metastatic cancer that shares molecular and clinical characteristics with human triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC), making it a relevant comparative model for a disease lacking targeted therapies. This study investigated the feasibility and clinical utility of 64CuCl2 PET/CT imaging in cats with naturally occurring mammary carcinoma. Eight cats (seven tumour-bearing, one healthy control) were administered an intravenous dose of 64CuCl2 and underwent whole-body PET/CT imaging. Semi-quantitative analysis was performed using standardized uptake values (SUVs), and tumour-to-muscle ratios were calculated to assess lesion conspicuity. Serum ceruloplasmin concentrations were measured as a marker of systemic copper metabolism. All primary masses were 64Cu-avid and conspicuous, with consistently elevated tumour-to-muscle ratios across tumour-bearing cats, allowing clear differentiation between neoplastic and normal tissue. Imaging provided additional staging information by identifying locally invasive and metastatic disease that was not fully evident on physical examination. Physiologic tracer distribution was characterized by high uptake in the liver and gallbladder and low uptake in skeletal muscle, which served as a reliable reference tissue. Serum ceruloplasmin concentrations varied widely and did not correlate with tumour uptake. These findings suggest that 64CuCl2 PET/CT is a feasible functional imaging modality for FMC, potentially aiding in tumour detection. This was an exploratory study, and not all imaging results could be confirmed by cytology or histopathology. Nonetheless, our findings suggest that 64CuCl2 PET/CT should be investigated further as a method for probing copper utilization in FMC.

papers.title: Medetomidine-vatinoxan is associated with a higher proportion of hypotension than dexmedetomidine in anesthetized dogs: a retrospective, matched-cohort study.
papers.authors: Rouse S, Muñoz K, Lerche P, Ballash G, Midon M, Aarnes TK, Pereira CHR
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To compare clinical parameters and medical interventions during the first hour of inhalant anesthesia in dogs administered medetomidine-vatinoxan (Zenalpha [ZEN]) versus dexmedetomidine (DEX) as IM preanesthetic agents. METHODS: Medical records were searched to identify dogs premedicated with ZEN between August 2022 and January 2025. Dogs administered DEX between July 2021 and May 2026 were then identified and matched with α2-adrenergic receptor agonist dose equivalence prioritized. Generalized estimating equation models were constructed to assess associations between variables of interest and premedication type, while accounting for repeated measurements within paired matched sets. RESULTS: The ZEN group included 24 dogs (ZEN dose median, 10 μg/kg; range, 5 to 26 μg/kg), whereas the DEX group included 48 dogs (DEX dose median, 5 μg/kg; range, 3 to 10 μg/kg), with no differences between groups. Compared with DEX, premedication with ZEN was associated with an 18 beats/min higher heart rate, whereas mean arterial pressure was 19 mm Hg lower. Dogs receiving ZEN had 9.3-fold greater odds of receiving an IV fluid bolus and 6.8-fold greater odds of vasopressor administration. No differences were detectable between groups in IV interventions administered for a light plane of anesthesia. CONCLUSIONS: Findings indicated ZEN was associated with intraoperative hypotension in dogs during the first hour of volatile anesthesia, despite significantly higher heart rates. This effect translated into a significantly greater need for hemodynamic intervention. CLINICAL RELEVANCE: The effects of ZEN on arterial blood pressure warrant careful hemodynamic monitoring and preparedness to provide blood pressure support in dogs undergoing inhalant anesthesia.

papers.title: Use of a cost-effective specimen retrieval bag for canine laparoscopic ovariectomy: a clinical prospective study (2021-2024).
papers.authors: Boullenger J, Gougeon E, Dunié-Mérigot A, Poncet C
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To assess the feasibility and safety of a cost-effective non-medical plastic bag used as a specimen retrieval bag during laparoscopic ovariectomy. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Thirty-one client-owned dogs having laparoscopic ovariectomy with a non-medical specimen retrieval bag were prospectively enrolled. A disposable liner for baby feeding bottles was used as a specimen retrieval bag. Each bag cost $1.3. Incision enlargement, surgical and retrieval times, retrieval easiness score, size of specimens, surgeon's status (resident or diplomate) and complications were recorded. Owner-assessed comfort score of their dogs and owners' satisfaction score were collected at 2 weeks postoperatively. RESULTS: The mean surgical time was 45.6 ± 13.4 minutes, and the mean retrieval time was 6.2 ± 4.4 minutes. The mean size of the specimens was 31.4 ± 19.2 mm. The median retrieval easiness score was 8.0 (IQR = 8.0 to 10.0) and was significantly lower for residents than diplomates (median difference = -1). Incision enlargement was required in three cases. Three minor intraoperative complications occurred. The median owner-assessed comfort score was 9.0 (IQR = 7.5 to 10.0) and the median owners' satisfaction score was 10.0 (IQR = 9.0 to 10.0). CLINICAL SIGNIFICANCE: Use of a sterilized non-medical plastic bag as specimen retrieval bag for canine laparoscopic ovariectomy was easy with limited minor complications, and excellent dogs' comfort and owners' satisfaction. It may be a suitable cost-effective alternative to commercial specimen retrieval bags for use in canine laparoscopic ovariectomy.

papers.title: Polarization Sensitive Optical Coherence Tomography for Surgical Margin Assessment for Canine Soft Tissue Sarcoma.
papers.authors: Patel N, Fontes G, Dornbusch J, Biggo M, Erickson A, Jurcak N, Mignucci JS, Shen YF, Weaver H, Jennings R
papers.abstract: Soft tissue sarcomas (STSs) and skeletal muscle both appear high scattering on spectral-domain optical coherence tomography (SD-OCT) imaging, which resulted in instances of misclassification by observers in prior soft tissue sarcoma margin assessment studies. Polarization-sensitive optical coherence tomography (PS-OCT) is an extension of OCT that provides additional information about tissue polarization contrast. In this prospective study we wanted to evaluate whether PS-OCT improves tissue differentiation and diagnostic accuracy compared to spectral-domain OCT (SD-OCT) alone. PS-OCT images from surgical margins of 10 resected STS were compared with histopathology to identify characteristic features of normal and neoplastic tissues. Then, six observers of varying OCT image interpretation experience assessed surgical margins from 30 resected STS using SD-OCT alone and SD-OCT combined with PS-OCT. PS-OCT images demonstrated distinct birefringence (optical patterns), corresponding to tissue organization: skeletal muscle exhibited alternating high and low birefringence bands, fascia showed variable birefringence and STS had uniformly low birefringence. Overall diagnostic accuracy was high for both modalities [correct classification rate: SD-OCT alone 93.7% (95% confidence interval (CI): 90.1, 96.0) vs. SD-OCT combined with PS-OCT 92.6% (95% = CI: 89.3, 95.4)]; adding PS-OCT did not significantly improve accuracy across all observers (p = 0.82), though expert observers benefited significantly (p = 0.0018). Interobserver and intraobserver agreement ranged from substantial to near perfect. These findings suggest PS-OCT can be interpreted reliably after brief training and may enhance accuracy for experienced users. Further research should explore structured training and real-time applications for comprehensive surgical margin evaluation.

papers.title: Generalized Megaesophagus Concurrent With Toxocariasis in a Cat.
papers.authors: Azargoun R, Hashemi-Asl SM, Hobbenaghi R, Malekifard F, Shamsaei B, Nabizadeh Z
papers.abstract: Feline megaesophagus is a rare disorder characterized by esophageal hypomotility and dilation, resulting in regurgitation, weight loss, and occasionally death. This report describes the clinical and paraclinical findings of generalized megaesophagus with a possible contribution of toxocariasis in a kitten. A 2-month-old female cat was referred with chief complaints of lethargy, hyporexia, dyspnea, and vomiting/regurgitation. Physical examination of the kitten revealed bradycardia, bradypnea, hypothermia, dehydration, and lung crackles. The most notable laboratory results were leukopenia with severe toxic changes in neutrophils. Radiographic findings were compatible with the diagnosis of generalized megaesophagus. Despite supportive measures, the kitten died the next day. Necropsy revealed diffuse esophageal dilation and Toxocara spp. roundworms in the stomach and duodenum. Histopathology showed an ascarid larva in the esophagus, necrosis and metaplasia in the pylorus, and absence of villi and Brunner's glands in the duodenum. Based on the morphological identification of the adult gastrointestinal nematodes, the final diagnosis was generalized megaesophagus of unspecified classification concurrent with toxocariasis. However, the exact cause of death could not be established. Although respiratory abnormalities raised suspicion of a pulmonary complication, pneumonia was not confirmed. We hypothesized that toxocariasis may have contributed to esophageal dysfunction in this kitten through potential mechanisms such as vomiting, gastrointestinal obstruction, or neurological involvement; however, these mechanisms could not be directly demonstrated. Therefore, parasitic diseases, including toxocariasis, may be considered among potential differential diagnoses or contributing conditions in young cats presenting with megaesophagus, particularly when concurrent gastrointestinal parasitism or related complications are identified. Further studies are required to clarify the possible relationship between toxocariasis and esophageal dysfunction.

papers.title: A novel 3D-printed patient-specific limb-sparing radial endoprosthesis for treatment of primary osteosarcoma in a Great Dane.
papers.authors: Tavola F, Kaczmarek J, Oxley B, Troedson K
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To describe a novel titanium three-dimensional-printed patient-specific radial endoprosthesis (3D-PSE) for the successful treatment of a primary osteosarcoma in a 7-year-old female Great Dane. STUDY DESIGN: Case report. METHODS: The dog presented with a 10-day history of swelling of the right distal radius. Computed tomography (CT) revealed an osteolytic lesion involving the distal metaphysis and diaphysis of the radius which was highly suspicious for an osteosarcoma (OSA). Thoracic CT showed no metastases. CT data was used to create a virtual 3D-model of the affected limb within computer-aided design software which was used for virtual osteotomy planning and the design of the 3D-PSE. During surgery 3D-printed patient-specific guides were used to execute osteotomies. The 3D-PSE comprised plate sections for attachment to the proximal radius and metacarpals 3, 4 and 5, and an integrated cage for bone graft to replace the radial defect. Histopathology demonstrated OSA, and postoperative adjuvant chemotherapy comprised five IV infusions of carboplatin every 3 weeks. The Liverpool Osteoarthritis in Dogs (LOAD) questionnaires were completed by the owner preoperatively and for each follow-up until the 6-month re-evaluation. RESULTS: No complications occurred intra-/post- or perioperatively. LOAD scores preoperatively, and at 6, 12 and 24 weeks postoperatively were 19, 13, 11 and 10. Ten months after surgery thoracic radiographs revealed multiple pulmonary metastases, but the dog remained asymptomatic for a further 6 weeks when progressive dyspnea and lethargy prompted euthanasia. Lameness was absent at that time. CONCLUSION: The described novel 3D-PSE provided an effective function-preserving solution as part of a multimodal treatment of a giant breed dog with OSA of the distal radius.

papers.title: Osteogenic priming of canine perivascular mesenchymal stromal cells enhances extracellular vesicle yield and in vitro activity for bone regeneration.
papers.authors: Hertel FC, da Silva AS, Spachi NB, Martins LMA, Rocha CC, Nolasco SCVM, do Amaral Xavier L, de Oliveira Silva J, de Barros ALB, Guimarães JD
papers.abstract: The therapeutic efficacy of mesenchymal stromal cells (MSCs) is intrinsically linked to their response to the host microenvironment by the interplay with resident cells. While MSC-derived extracellular vesicles (EVs) offer a promising cell-free alternative, optimizing their production and cargo for specific clinical applications remains a challenge. We investigated the impact of in vitro osteogenic priming on the yield, molecular profile, and functional activity of EVs derived from canine umbilical cord perivascular MSCs (cPMSCs). The EVs secreted by osteogenic primed and naïve cPMSC were isolated by ultracentrifugation and characterized by nanoparticle tracking analysis, western blotting, and electronic transmission microscopy. In vitro functional assays of cellular uptake, proliferation, migration, and mineralization were performed. MicroRNAs known to participate in osteogenesis (cfa-miR-21, cfa-miR26a, cfa-miR-27a and cfa-miR-29a) were evaluated in EV samples of both groups through RT-qPCR. Notably, osteogenic priming led to a 1.5-fold increase in vesicle yield (5.6 ± 0.5 ×1010 particles/mL) compared to naïve MSCs (3.7 ± 0.7 ×1010 particles/mL), without altering vesicle distribution nor TSG101 expression (similar expression for both groups). Functional assays revealed that while both EV populations were efficiently internalized, osteogenic priming significantly improved extracellular matrix mineralization (P = 0.0003) and enhanced EV-mediated cell migration (P = 0.005). Molecular analysis confirmed the enrichment of key osteogenic microRNAs, including cfa-miR-21, cfa-miR-26a, cfa-miR-27a, and cfa-miR-29a, in both groups. These findings demonstrate that osteogenic priming is a robust strategy to improve EV production efficiency and migratory potential, providing a molecularly characterized foundation for advanced cell-free orthopedic therapies in veterinary medicine.

papers.title: Comparison of peribulbar anesthesia with neosaxitoxin or bupivacaine in dogs undergoing reconstructive keratoplasty.
papers.authors: Ribeiro MR, Ariga BK, Gomes DR, Alves DS, Andrade SF, Reed RA, Barletta M, Cassu RN
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: This study compared the analgesic efficacy of peribulbar anesthesia using neosaxitoxin versus bupivacaine in dogs undergoing reconstructive keratoplasty. METHODS: Of 28 dogs, four were excluded for not meeting the inclusion criteria. The anesthetic protocol included dexmedetomidine and methadone, propofol and isoflurane. Immediately after intubation, 24 dogs were randomly assigned (12 per group) to receive peribulbar block with either neosaxitoxin (3.5 µg; NeoSTX group) or 0.5% bupivacaine (0.2 mL/kg, Bupi group). Intraoperatively, cardiopulmonary variables and end-tidal isoflurane concentration (FE'ISO) were recorded at predefined time points. Pain, corneal esthesiometry, blepharospasm, and sedation were assessed preoperatively and up to 24 h post-extubation. Methadone was administered as rescue analgesia. The duration of analgesia, defined as the interval between block administration and the first rescue analgesia, was also recorded. RESULTS: Cardiopulmonary parameters, blepharospasm, duration of analgesia and sedation scores did not differ between treatments. The area under the curve (AUC) of Fe´ISO and esthesiometry were lower in the NeoSTX group compared to the Bupi group (P = 0.004; P = 0.009, respectively). Pain was lower in the Bupi group at 12 h post-extubation compared with the NeoSTX group (P = 0.012). Methadone was required in 4/12 dogs in each group, administered at 4-6 h post-extubation in the Bupi group and at 12-18 h in the NeoSTX group. CONCLUSION: In conclusion, at the dose and concentrations used in this study, peribulbar NeoSTX was associated with lower isoflurane and corneal esthesiometry AUCs, but did not provide additional postoperative analgesic benefit compared with bupivacaine.

papers.title: Point-of-care troponin I assay has acceptable performance detecting clinically important canine myocardial injury but reduced precision at low concentrations.
papers.authors: Ditzler B, Saunders AB, Wesselowski S, Guadiano P, Dunham JW, Lidbury JA
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To perform a partial validation of a point-of-care assay (Vcheck cardiac troponin I [VC-cTnI; cTnI]) for measurement of cTnI in canine serum and to perform a method comparison between the VC-cTnI and an established chemiluminescent assay (ADVIA Centaur XP High-Sensitivity Troponin I [AC-cTnI-HS]). METHODS: From September 4, 2024, through August 21, 2025, surplus canine serum was collected from a diagnostic laboratory, and within-day variability, dilutional parallelism, spiking recovery, and the effect of common interferents (hemolysis, icterus, and lipemia) were analyzed for the VC-cTnI assay. A method comparison of the VC-cTnI and AC-cTnI-HS assays was performed with 121 canine serum samples. RESULTS: The within-day coefficient of variation ranged from 8.1% to 43.8%, decreasing as cTnI concentrations increased. Dilutional parallelism and spiking recovery assessments had mean ± SD observed-to-expected ratios of 80.5 ± 33.2% (range, 21.1% to 122.2%) and 112.8 ± 35.6% (range, 46.0% to 173.9%), respectively. There was no interference from icterus, hemolysis, or lipemia. There was a positive correlation between the VC-cTnI and AC-cTnI-HS assays (Spearman ρ, 0.742), though 16 of 121 samples (13.2%) were below the VC-cTnI detectable limit. CONCLUSIONS: The VC-cTnI assay lacked precision for measurement of concentrations below 0.2 ng/mL, but within-day variability was acceptable for higher concentrations. CLINICAL RELEVANCE: The VC-cTnI assay is more precise when measuring higher cTnI concentrations and can detect myocardial injury in dogs. Results in the normal and equivocal range of the manufacturer's reference interval may be more challenging to interpret because of suboptimal precision in this range.

papers.title: Evaluation of nanofibrillated cellulose as a urethral bulking agent in female dogs with acquired urethral sphincter mechanism incompetence: a prospective clinical study.
papers.authors: Peltokallio NMM, Bolen G, Gordin E, Lepajõe J, Hamaide A, Laitinen-Vapaavuori OM, Noël S
papers.abstract: Urethral bulking agent (UBA) implantation is a minimally invasive, effective and safe alternative treatment for refractory urethral sphincter mechanism incompetence (USMI). However, repeated implantations are frequently needed to maintain continence. Therefore, a prospective interventional clinical study with eight client-owned neutered female dogs was designed to evaluate the clinical efficacy and 12-month outcome of nanofibrillated cellulose (NFC), a novel biomaterial as a UBA. Concurrent causes of urinary incontinence were excluded with clinical and neurological assessment, blood and urine sampling, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), retrograde vaginourethrography, cystoscopy, and urodynamic testing. A continence score (CS) was assigned before and after treatment, and monthly thereafter. Furthermore, the dogs were followed with MRI, retrograde vaginouretrography, and urethroscopy at 1 and 12 months or at the time of euthanasia or recurrence. All dogs were continent (CS ≥ 8/10) at 1 month with a significant increase in mean CS (p < 0.0001, difference 5.4, 95% CI 4.1-6.6). Median duration of continence was 8 months (IQR 4 - not estimable). At 12 months, the treatment response was still significant (p = 0.0010) with (n = 4/7) or without (n = 3/7) medical intervention. The imaging and urethroscopy findings suggest that flattening of the deposits with or without mucosal ulceration may contribute to recurrence. Sporadic bacterial cystitis was diagnosed in two dogs and recurrent cystitis in one. In conclusion, NFC showed promising short-term effect and a low complication rate when used as a UBA. Urinary incontinence resolved after single NFC implantation in all dogs for a median of 8 months without adjunctive treatment.

papers.title: The effects of low-dose medetomidine and butorphanol premedication on anesthetic induction and recovery for intramuscular alfaxalone anesthesia in cats.
papers.authors: Tanaka K, Shinozaki H, Tamura J, Oyama N, Sano T, Itoh A, Itami T, Yamashita K
papers.abstract: This study evaluated effects of premedication with low-dose medetomidine (MED), butorphanol (BTR), or their combination on intramuscular (IM) alfaxalone (ALFX) anesthesia in cats. Five healthy purpose-bred cats were used in a completely randomized crossover study with a minimum 1-week washout period. Cats received three types of premedication: MED (5 µg/kg), BTR (0.3 mg/kg) or their combination via IM injection. After 15 min, anesthesia was induced with low (1.0 mg/kg), medium (2.5 mg/kg) or high (5.0 mg/kg) doses of IM ALFX. Anesthetic depth, tracheal intubation scores, and cardiorespiratory variables were evaluated over 120 min. Dose-dependent anesthetic effects of ALFX were observed across all protocols. Although tracheal intubation was difficult with MED alone, premedication with BTR alone or in combination with MED facilitated successful intubation. Notably, the MED-BTR combination resulted in a significantly greater sedation/anesthetic effect, even with lower doses of ALFX. The MED-BTR combination completely prevented MED-induced emesis. Cardiorespiratory evaluation revealed a decrease in heart rate with MED and MED-BTR premedication, and percutaneous arterial oxygen saturation dropped below 93% temporarily at higher ALFX doses. In summary, premedication combining BTR and low-dose MED facilitates reliable and smooth anesthetic induction with low-dose ALFX (1.0 mg/kg), achieving sufficient anesthetic depth without inducing prolonged or turbulent recovery. However, careful monitoring for bradycardia and hypoxemia is recommended, and its clinical application should be limited to young and healthy cats with sufficient cardiorespiratory reserve.

papers.title: Clinical features, management, short- and long-term outcomes for cats and dogs diagnosed with pyothorax: 103 cases (2015-2021).
papers.authors: Bartlett AJ, Dordio AM, Jerabkova P, Sparks T, Herrtage M
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To describe canine and feline pyothorax cases, comparing bacteriology, aetiologies and short- and long-term outcomes of medical versus surgical treatment. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Clinical records of canine and feline pyothorax cases from two UK referral centres (2015 to 2021) were retrospectively reviewed. Follow-up was obtained from referring practices' records. RESULTS: Sixty-five dogs and 38 cats were included. Medical management was used in 62% of dogs (40/65) and 76% of cats (29/38); survival to discharge was 88% (35/40) and 90% (26/29), respectively. Surgery was performed in the remainder; survival to discharge was 80% (20/25) in dogs and 78% (7/9) in cats. Among cases with follow-up, recurrence was 8% (4/51) in dogs: 5% (1/19) surgically and 9% (3/32) medically managed; and 8% (2/24) in cats: 12% (2/17) medically managed. All dogs medically managed with thoracostomy tubes receiving pleural lavage survived: 100% (16/16) versus 73% (8/11) without. Pasteurella multocida was the predominant feline isolate, in contrast to dogs that had no single dominant species. Multidrug-resistant organisms were identified in 29% (7/24) and 21% (5/24) of culture-positive canine and feline patients. Aetiologies were mostly unknown (dogs: 51%, 33/65; cats: 61%, 23/38), followed by parapneumonic spread (dogs: 17%, 11/65; cats: 16%, 6/38) and migrating foreign bodies (dogs: 17%, 11/65; cats: 8%, 3/38). CLINICAL SIGNIFICANCE: In selected cases, medical management of canine and feline pyothorax with thoracic drains yields survival to discharge and recurrence rates comparable to surgery, including cases with suspected migrating plant material. Pleural lavage during medical management is associated with improved survival in dogs.

papers.title: Low complication rates are reported in cats presenting for neurological complaints and undergoing cerebrospinal fluid collection.
papers.authors: Spinoglio GJ, Korman R, Thompson AL
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To assess complications, outcomes, and associated risk factors of cats undergoing CSF collection. METHODS: This was a single-center retrospective cohort study of client-owned cats presenting to 3 referral hospitals for CSF collection from January 2012 through December 2022. Cats were excluded for nonspecific and/or extraneural presenting complaints. If cats had multiple CSF collection presentations, only the first was included. Records were retrospectively assessed for signalment, physical examination findings, modified Glasgow coma scale, general anesthesia (GA) records, diagnostic imaging, clinical pathology results, and suspected or confirmed final diagnosis. Outcomes included complications and nonsurvival > 24 hours following CSF collection. Univariable logistic regression included breed, sex, body weight, age, modified Glasgow coma scale, evidence of herniation, evidence of intracranial hypertension (ICH) without herniation, GA protocol, GA duration, CSF analysis, collection site, inflammatory/infectious, and neoplasia diagnosis. P values were adjusted for multiple comparisons using the Benjamini-Hochberg procedure. RESULTS: 120 cats were identified, with 2 excluded for nonspecific and/or extraneural presenting complaint, leaving 118 cats. Seven (5.9%) did not survive > 24 hours following CSF procedure, and 9 (7.6%) reported complications, including apnea, suspected iatrogenic spinal cord trauma, and Cushing reflex. After multiple-comparison correction, no variable was significantly associated with outcome. Evidence of ICH without herniation and nonsurvival reported the largest effect estimate (OR, 36.99). Estimates are imprecise and reported as hypothesis generating. CONCLUSIONS: Feline CSF collection in this cohort reported low complication rates, and the majority survived > 24 hours after CSF collection. CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Imaging review for abnormalities associated with ICH is recommended prior to CSF collection.

papers.title: Two headless cannulated screws have a higher maximum failure load than screw-and-pin fixation at a 70° fracture angle in 3-dimensionally printed canine femoral neck models.
papers.authors: Song I, Kim S, Kim HY, Kim JM
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To compare maximum failure load among 3-D-printed canine femoral neck models differing in fracture angle and fixation configuration. METHODS: This experimental biomechanical study was conducted in a university research laboratory from September 10, 2025, through March 10, 2026. Polycarbonate 3-D-printed models were created using left femoral CT data from a 2-year-old 11.9-kg Shiba Inu. The group configurations were a 50° femoral neck fracture stabilized with one 2.5-mm fully threaded headless cannulated screw (HCS) and an antirotation pin (1S1P50), a 70° fracture with the same fixation (1S1P70), and a 70° fracture stabilized with 2 parallel 2.5-mm HCSs (2S70). Initial construct stiffness was estimated from load-crosshead displacement curves. Maximum failure load, the primary outcome, was determined under single axial compression of the femoral head. RESULTS: 18 models were analyzed, with 6 in each group. There was no difference in initial construct stiffness among groups. Mean maximum failure loads were 511.5 N (SD, 81.9) in 1S1P50, 502.0 N (SD, 47.2) in 1S1P70, and 679.2 N (SD, 102.5) in 2S70. Maximum failure load was higher in 2S70 than in 1S1P70 (estimated difference, 176 N; Bonferroni-adjusted 98.3% CI, 31 to 301 N). CONCLUSIONS: Under static axial loading, 2S70 had a higher maximum failure load than 1S1P70, with no difference between 1S1P50 and either of the other 2 groups. CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Under static axial loading, 2 HCSs had a higher maximum failure load than did 1 HCS with an antirotation pin at a 70° fracture angle in 3-D-printed canine femoral neck models.

papers.title: Usefulness of serum amyloid A to differentiate feline inflammatory lower respiratory tract diseases from cardiac or neoplastic disease: a retrospective study of 22 cats (2021-2024).
papers.authors: Berro E, Fastrès A, Lamoureux A
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the usefulness of serum amyloid A concentration in differentiating inflammatory lower respiratory tract diseases from cardiac/neoplastic respiratory diseases in cats. METHODS: A retrospective analysis of medical records of cats presented between 2021 and 2024 to a single referral centre was performed. Cats in respiratory distress with serum amyloid A assay performed within 48 hours after admission were included and divided into two groups (inflammatory and cardiac/neoplastic). The inflammatory group included infectious or non-infectious inflammatory lower respiratory tract diseases, and the cardiac/neoplastic group was subdivided into cardiac and neoplastic subgroups. Signalment, clinical signs and diagnostic testing results, including serum amyloid A concentration, were recorded and compared between groups (P < .05). RESULTS: Twenty-two cats were included. Median serum amyloid A concentration was significantly higher in the inflammatory group (57.5 μg/mL (12.2 to 70.3); n = 15) compared to the cardiac/neoplastic group (5 μg/mL (5); n = 7; P = .003). There was also a significant difference among the inflammatory, cardiac (5 μg/mL (5); n = 3) and N (5 μg/mL (5); n = 4) subgroups (P = .01); however, pairwise comparisons were not statistically significant. The optimal serum amyloid A concentration cut-off to differentiate between inflammatory and cardiac/neoplastic groups was 8.6 μg/mL (sensitivity of 80% (95% confidence interval: 59.5 to 91.6) and specificity of 100% (95% confidence interval: 84.6 to 100)). CLINICAL SIGNIFICANCE: Cardiac and neoplastic diseases were associated with low serum amyloid A concentration. Serum amyloid A concentration could be a potential diagnostic tool but larger studies are needed to validate the proposed cut-off value. Further prospective studies are also needed to establish the usefulness of serum amyloid A concentration in distinguishing between infectious and non-infectious inflammatory diseases.

papers.title: Biomechanical evaluation of cerclage fixation constructs in a 3-dimensionally printed canine tibial long-oblique fracture model.
papers.authors: Park J, Kim JM, Kim HY
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To compare the biomechanical performance of cerclage fixation constructs in a standardized 3-D-printed canine tibial long-oblique fracture model. METHODS: 3 fixation constructs-stainless steel wire cerclage (SSW), FiberWire cerclage (FW), and paraosseous clamp-cerclage stabilization (PCCS)-were compared in a standardized 3-D-printed canine tibial long-oblique fracture model. A standardized mid-diaphyseal long-oblique fracture was created in each specimen. Axial compression testing was performed until failure. Loads required to reach predefined displacement levels (1, 2, and 3 mm), maximum failure load, and failure mode were recorded. Data were analyzed using one-way ANOVA with the Tukey post hoc test. RESULTS: 21 tibial models (7/group) were evaluated. At all displacement levels, the FW group required significantly lower loads than both the SSW and PCCS groups, whereas no significant difference was observed between the SSW and PCCS groups. Mean loads at 1 mm displacement were 194.5 ± 32.2 N (SSW), 94.4 ± 21.0 N (FW), and 207.3 ± 64.0 N (PCCS). Maximum failure load was highest in the FW group (974.3 ± 77.0 N), followed by the PCCS group (879.0 ± 66.6 N) and SSW group (567.6 ± 63.2 N). CONCLUSIONS: PCCS demonstrated resistance to axial compression comparable to SSW fixation, whereas FW cerclage demonstrated the highest maximum failure load. CLINICAL RELEVANCE: These findings provide biomechanical information that may assist surgeons in selecting cerclage fixation methods for long-oblique tibial fractures in dogs.

papers.title: Clinical features, survival, and associated factors for canine mast cell tumors: The role of neutering.
papers.authors: da Silva EMG, Mantovani MM, Silva MJB
papers.abstract: Canine mast cell tumors are among the most common skin neoplasms in dogs and exhibit highly variable biological behavior. Several factors have been associated with their development and prognosis, including breed, body size, and histological grade; however, the influence of neutering status, particularly age at neutering, on the odds of tumor diagnosis and survival remains unclear. This study aimed to evaluate clinical features, factors associated with diagnosis, and survival outcomes in dogs with mast cell tumors (MCTs), with emphasis on neutering status and age at neutering. A retrospective case-control and survival study was conducted using medical records of dogs treated at a university veterinary hospital from 2015 to 2024. Dogs diagnosed with MCT were included as cases and compared with tumor-free controls matched by age category. Epidemiological, clinical, and pathological variables were analyzed, and agreement between cytological and histopathological grading was assessed. Among 56,254 dogs evaluated during the study period, 313 were diagnosed with MCT. Neutering before 24 months of age was associated with increased odds of MCT diagnosis compared with intact dogs, whereas neutering after 24 months of age was not. Medium and large body size, overweight body condition score, and specific breeds, particularly American Pit Bull Terriers and Boxers, were also associated with tumor diagnosis. In survival analysis, histological grade and tumor size were associated with survival time, whereas neutering status was not.

papers.title: Long-term outcomes following modified Blalock-Taussig-Thomas shunt placement in 13 dogs with cyanotic congenital heart disease.
papers.authors: Rossanese M, Hannabuss J, Brockman D
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To describe long-term outcome and owner-perceived quality of life in dogs with cyanotic congenital cardiac disease undergoing modified Blalock-Taussig-Thomas shunt procedure. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Medical records of dogs that underwent Blalock-Taussig-Thomas shunt between 2009 and 2025 at a small animal referral hospital were retrospectively reviewed. Complications, long-term outcomes and quality of life were assessed via clinical examination and/or contact with owners or referring veterinarians. RESULTS: Thirteen dogs were included. The predominant clinical signs were exercise intolerance, cyanosis and a heart murmur. Diagnosis included tetralogy of Fallot (n = 8), double outlet right ventricle (n = 3); tetralogy of Fallot-double outlet right ventricle spectrum (n = 1) and tetralogy of Fallot with pulmonary atresia spectrum (n = 1). All dogs survived surgery. Follow-up was available for 12 dogs, ranging from 58 to 2094 days. Eight dogs died or were euthanased for cardiac-related reasons, three were alive at follow-up and one dog was alive 278 days after surgery at last point of contact. All dogs showed a marked postoperative clinical improvement. Shunt obstruction or partial obstruction was documented in three of 12 dogs at 265, 587 and 693 days. Postoperative balloon valvuloplasty was performed in three of the 12 dogs, one died during the procedure and two dogs showed clinical improvement and extended good quality survival. Owners' perception of the procedure outcome and quality of life was described as good, with only mild adjustments needed for exercise. CLINICAL SIGNIFICANCE: Blalock-Taussig-Thomas shunt is an effective palliative option for dogs with cyanotic congenital cardiac diseases associated with reduced pulmonary blood flow, providing sustained clinical improvement and quality of life. Recurrence of clinical signs could indicate shunt obstruction and warrants prompt assessment.

papers.title: Oral trazodone alone or in combination with gabapentin reduces the expression of stress-related behaviors in a randomized controlled trial with shelter dogs.
papers.authors: Delabar A, Koch CS, Burling A, Wallace L, Middleton JR
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To determine the effects of oral trazodone and gabapentin on the expression of stress-related behaviors (SRBs) in shelter dogs. METHODS: SRBs were compared among shelter dogs treated orally with trazodone (8 mg/kg), gabapentin (25 mg/kg), trazodone (8 mg/kg) with gabapentin (25 mg/kg), or neither (control) the evening before and the morning of surgical neuter (ovariohysterectomy or castration). Dogs were enrolled between September 2020 and October 2021. Video recordings captured the behavior at baseline, 14 hours after the first treatment, and 1.5 hours after the second treatment. Fifteen SRBs were scored independently by blinded observers as present (1) or absent (0). Minute 1 recordings were in the absence of a person, and minute 2 recordings were in the presence of a person. The final SRB score was the sum of scores assigned by each observer at each time point, ranging from no SRB to 15 SRBs. RESULTS: 60 dogs and 13 SRBs were included in the final analysis. Mean behavior score was lower at minute 1 than minute 2 at baseline, the trazodone and combination groups had a significant reduction in mean behavior score, and the gabapentin group had an increase in mean behavior score. Mean scores in the control group did not differ over time. CONCLUSIONS: Oral trazodone alone or with gabapentin prior to surgery may be beneficial in reducing SRBs in shelter dogs. CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Oral trazodone alone or in combination with gabapentin may be useful in mitigating SRBs in dogs during veterinary care and related procedures.

papers.title: Predictors of carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales enteric colonization among patients admitted to a companion animal intensive care unit.
papers.authors: Hidalgo Montealegre D, King CA, Mollenkopf DF, Van Balen JC, Cooper ES, Wittum TE, Diaz-Campos D
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To estimate prevalence and identify factors associated with carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales (CRE) enteric colonization in companion animals admitted to an ICU. METHODS: The study population included canine and feline patients admitted to The Ohio State University Veterinary Medical Center ICU between January 2024 and June 2025. In total, 5,552 rectal swabs were collected from 3,834 patients during routine screening. A retrospective case-control study included all CRE-positive patients (n = 61) and randomly selected CRE-negative controls (137). Cases were defined as ICU patients with at least 1 positive CRE fecal culture during hospitalization, whereas controls had no positive CRE fecal cultures during their hospitalization. RESULTS: Prevalence of CRE colonization was 1.59% (61 of 3,834 patients; 95% CI, 1.24% to 2.04%). Escherichia coli carrying blaNDM was the most frequently identified isolate, accounting for 78.7% (48 of 61 patients; 95% CI, 66.9% to 87.1%). Predictors of CRE colonization included increased comorbidity burden (unit OR, 1.96; 95% CI, 1.43 to 2.75), intact reproductive status (OR, 4.39; CI, 1.47 to 11.03), longer hospitalization (unit OR, 1.31; CI, 1.14 to 1.53), recent surgery (OR, 2.72; CI, 1.29 to 5.87), and antimicrobial use within the previous 3 months (OR, 2.71; CI, 1.23 to 6.07). CONCLUSIONS: These predictors suggest targets for infection prevention and control measures to protect patients and staff. The association between recent antimicrobial exposure and CRE colonization reinforces the importance of antimicrobial stewardship in veterinary medicine. CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Although uncommon, CRE-colonized patients can serve as reservoirs for transmission and are at risk of subsequent infection.

papers.title: Transdiaphragmatic video-assisted lobectomy of caudal and accessory lung lobes: A canine cadaveric feasibility study.
papers.authors: Rico-Holgado S, Garcia-Pertierra S, Martinez-Trapero A, Pera-Serrano M, Fontalba-Navas JL, Calvo I
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the feasibility and technical outcomes of a video-assisted transdiaphragmatic (VATD) approach to perform total lung lobectomy of the caudal and accessory pulmonary lobes in canine cadavers. STUDY DESIGN: Cadaveric study. ANIMALS: A total of 12 canine cadavers. METHODS: Cadavers were randomly assigned to left caudal, right caudal or accessory lung lobectomy (n = 4/group). A cranial midline celiotomy and transdiaphragmatic approach were performed with rigid videoendoscopic assistance under standardized procedural conditions. Lobectomies were completed using an endoscopic linear stapler. Recorded variables included achievement of complete pulmonary lobectomy, surgical times, incision length, and intraoperative technical events. Staple-line integrity was assessed using an air leak test. Descriptive statistics and logistic regression were used to evaluate results and associations with cadaver weight and body condition score (BCS). RESULTS: Total lobectomy was achieved in 11/12 cadavers (91.7%), including all caudal lobes (100%) and three accessory lobes (75%). Mean total surgical time was 65.6 ± 26.8 min and incision length represented approximately one-third of abdominal midline length. Air leaks were identified in two accessory lung lobe lobectomies. No other intraoperative technical events were recorded. Two staple cartridges were required in 4/12 procedures (33.3%). Procedural success was not associated with cadaver weight or BCS. CONCLUSION: A VATD approach was feasible in canine cadavers and allowed total resection of caudal lung lobes, with slightly lower success for the accessory lung lobe. CLINICAL RELEVANCE: A VATD approach provided effective hilar exposure and acceptable procedural times in this cadaveric model. Further investigation in clinical patients is required to determine safety and clinical applicability and perioperative outcomes in dogs accurately.

papers.title: Gastrointestinal transit time of healthy dogs before and after enema assessed by contrast radiographs with barium-impregnated polyethylene spheres.
papers.authors: de Souza MR, da Silva WPR, Xavier RAL, da Silva CCL, Ruiz KC, de Vicente MC, da Silva RHS, Martins DB, Borges NC, Botelho AFM
papers.abstract: In this prospective experimental study, we aimed to assess the gastrointestinal (GI) transit of healthy dogs with and without an enema, using barium-impregnated polyethylene spheres (BIPS). Six healthy dogs underwent two experimental steps: evaluation of the GI transit using BIPS (BIPS group) before and after enema (BIPS+ENEMA group). All animals were fasted for 12 h, the transit was assessed in serial radiographs from 0 to 12 h, and BIPS were counted in each segment of the GI tract, calculating the gastric emptying time and the time the spheres reached the descending colon. Blood cell count, serum biochemistry, electrolytes, and blood glucose levels were assessed during the experiment to evaluate the safety of both BIPs and enema. BIPS were easily identified in all segments of the GI tract. The BIPS group presented gastric emptying starting at H0 and H1, ending around H8. BIPS + ENEMA group showed a delayed gastric emptying, which began around H1 and extended to more than H12, and had a lower percentage of spheres in the descending colon at the end of the evaluation; however, the differences were not statistically significant. BIPS and enema did not cause changes in laboratory evaluation, and the 12-hour fast did not cause hypoglycemia. Based on the findings, when using BIPS for radiographic contrast, an enema is not a required procedure. The use of the enema and BIPS can be considered safe, with no apparent adverse effects in dogs.

papers.title: Echocardiographic changes in hyperthyroid cats: Comparison of subclinical disease and congestive heart failure.
papers.authors: Greil S, Utzinger H, Maerz I
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Hyperthyroidism induces a wide spectrum of cardiovascular changes in cats, yet the factors distinguishing subclinical cardiac involvement from congestive heart failure (CHF) remain poorly defined. Previous studies have focused primarily on structural changes, with limited evaluation of atrial function or right-sided involvement. OBJECTIVES: To compare echocardiographic variables between hyperthyroid cats with subclinical cardiac disease and those presenting in CHF, with emphasis on left atrial remodelling, left atrial function, and left ventricular dimensional changes, and right-sided involvement assessed by right atrial diameter. The comparison of clinical and biochemical variables was a secondary objective. METHODS: A retrospective case-control study was performed using medical records of 51 hyperthyroid cats with subclinical cardiac disease and 47 hyperthyroid cats presenting in CHF. All cats underwent standard echocardiography, serum biochemistry including total thyroxine (TT4). Type of congestion was determined by thoracic radiography or point-of-care ultrasound, and CHF cats were classified as having pulmonary oedema only or pleural/mixed effusion. RESULTS: Cats with CHF had significantly larger atrial dimensions and increased left ventricular internal diameter compared with subclinical cats. Left atrial dysfunction was the most robust discriminator between groups. Pleural or mixed effusion was the predominant CHF phenotype and, compared with pulmonary oedema alone, was associated with greater right-sided and global volume overload. TT4 concentrations did not differ significantly between cats with and without CHF. Similarly, biochemical variables showed no significant differences between subclinical or CHF cats or between CHF subtypes. CONCLUSIONS: Atrial remodelling - particularly impaired atrial function and biatrial enlargement - represents the clearest echocardiographic marker of decompensation in hyperthyroid cats. The predominance of pleural or mixed effusion highlights the importance of assessing right-sided cardiac measurements. Comprehensive echocardiographic evaluation is essential for early identification of cats at risk of CHF, whereas TT4 concentration alone does not predict cardiac status.

papers.title: Survey of the health and welfare of imported dogs presenting to UK veterinary surgeons.
papers.authors: Pinchbeck G, Lyne R, Wallis L, Stavisky J, Christley R, Buckley L, Westgarth C
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Since changes to legislation in 2012, numbers of dogs imported into the UK, especially rescues, have increased substantially. We aimed to explore the health and behaviour issues among imported dogs presented to UK veterinary surgeons. METHODS: An online survey was completed by 413 veterinary surgeons practising in the UK in 2023. The findings were analysed with descriptive statistics. RESULTS: Thirteen percent had encountered imported dogs who had died during or shortly after transportation and two-thirds reported observing dogs they considered were unfit to travel, including dogs with unhealed wounds and fractures. Common behavioural concerns included fear of people, noises or objects, and unwanted behaviours when confined or alone. The most common infectious diseases reported as being diagnosed were leishmaniasis, dirofilariasis and brucellosis. Suspected falsified health documentation or passports had been observed by almost two-thirds of respondents. Less than half of respondents reported specific practice policies or testing protocols for exotic diseases. LIMITATIONS: This convenience sample is limited by what is presented to veterinary surgeons and recall over the previous 24 months. CONCLUSION: Participants reported significant welfare concerns in current dog importation practices and highlighted a need for clearer guidance on management and treatment of imported dogs in veterinary practice.

papers.title: Exploratory Retrospective Study on Rehabilitation in Dogs Affected by Acute Idiopathic Polyradiculoneuritis.
papers.authors: Bruno E, Salvador E, Balducci F, Antonucci M, Dalmonte T, Spinella G
papers.abstract: Acute Canine Idiopathic Polyradiculoneuritis (ACIP) is one of the most common acute-onset peripheral neuropathies in dogs. Since there is no specific therapy, rehabilitation represents the main supporting treatment for canine patients. This exploratory retrospective study analyzes the role and effectiveness of physiotherapy rehabilitation in the treatment of ACIP, evaluating the recovery times of spontaneous walking ability and potential correlation between the considered variables that could influence its progress. The study included 12 clinical cases affected by ACIP and submitted to a physiotherapy support plan for independent gait recovery. Patients were divided into two groups on the basis of the number of rehabilitation sessions required for spontaneous ambulation achievement: less than 40 (Group A) and more than 40 sessions (Group B). Statistical analysis showed no significant association between qualitative variables. Given the inherent methodological limitations and small cohort size, these preliminary findings should be interpreted with caution. However, the data tentatively suggest that intensive rehabilitation strategies might support a more rapid recovery of independent ambulation, even though the number of moderate and maintenance sessions did not differ significantly between the groups. Consequently, further studies with statistical power are required to confirm these trends.

papers.title: Vitamin D supplementation in dogs with chronic biliary tract diseases.
papers.authors: Habermaass V, Cogozzo A, Bartoli F, Rocca DJ, Dini R, Puccinelli C, Marchetti V
papers.abstract: Extrahepatic cholestasis in dogs is frequently associated with reduced intestinal absorption of fat-soluble vitamins, resulting in suboptimal vitamin D status. This prospective longitudinal study assessed the effects of six-week oral cholecalciferol supplementation (40 IU/kg/day) on serum 25-hydroxycholecalciferol [25(OH)D] in fourteen dogs with chronic biliary disease. Median baseline 25(OH)D concentration was 2.3 ng/mL (0.3-11.2), increasing to 4.3 ng/mL (2.4-14.0) after treatment, whereas healthy controls (n = 31) showed 11.68 ng/mL (2.65-37.93). Statistical analyses (paired Wilcoxon tests) confirmed a significant increase post-supplementation (p = 0.003). Ionized calcium and phosphorus levels were stable, and no hypercalcemia occurred. Biochemical parameters (alkaline phosphatase, alanine aminotransferase, gamma-glutamyl transferase, cholesterol, total bilirubin) showed nonsignificant downward trends, indicating good hepatic tolerance. Cholecalciferol supplementation was thus safe and effectively improved vitamin D status, although concentrations remained lower than those observed in the study's healthy controls. The heterogeneous response suggests variable intestinal absorption or disease severity. Further controlled, long-term studies are needed to refine dosing strategies and clarify potential hepatic and clinical benefits.

papers.title: Longitudinal assessment of left and right ventricular systolic function in dogs undergoing chemotherapy with doxorubicin.
papers.authors: Wolf M, Lucina SB, Silva VBC, Silveira MF, Silva VG, Kano N, Sarraff AP, de Cássia Custódio C, da Costa BN, Sousa MG
papers.abstract: Cardiotoxicity is a recognized complication of chemotherapy with doxorubicin and is classically associated with left ventricular dysfunction; however, evidence from human cardio-oncology suggests that global cardiac function, including the right ventricle, may also be affected, and that advanced echocardiographic techniques such as global longitudinal strain (GLS) and tissue motion annular displacement (TMAD) may detect subtle myocardial dysfunction earlier than conventional indices. This prospective longitudinal study evaluated 25 dogs with cancer undergoing doxorubicin chemotherapy, administered alone or in combination with other drugs, using conventional echocardiography and speckle tracking before treatment and at 7, 21, 60, 120 and 180 days after the first dose. Twelve dogs completed all evaluations. No significant changes were observed over time in left ventricular volumes, fractional shortening, ejection fraction, global circumferential strain or GLS. However, reductions in MAPSEi lateral (P = 0.002), MAPSEi septal (P = 0.0293) and global TMAD% (P = 0.046) were observed at 180 days compared with baseline, along with decreased E' wave velocity and a negative correlation between cumulative doxorubicin dose and the E:A ratio, suggesting a dose-dependent effect on diastolic function. In the right ventricle, progressive reductions in TAPSEi (P < 0.001), RV S'n wave (P = 0.036), FAC (P = 0.04), RV GLS (P = 0.002) and RV TMAD (P = 0.019) were observed over time. These findings indicate subclinical reductions in indices of systolic function of both ventricles, highlighting the sensitivity of MAPSE, TAPSE and TMAD for early detection of myocardial alterations. papers.title: EXPRESS: Assessment of caregiver burden in feline chronic kidney disease.
papers.authors: Lim L, Quimby JM, Caney S
papers.abstract: ObjectivesThe aim of this study was to investigate caregiver burden associated with management of cats with chronic kidney disease (CKD).MethodsCaregivers who had experience managing a cat with CKD were recruited through social media to anonymously participate in an online Qualtrics survey. The modified Zarit Burden Interview (mZBI) was incorporated into the survey to objectively assess caregiver burden. An mZBI score of ≥ 18 represents clinically significant burden.ResultsA total of 339 surveys were completed. 46% of caregivers reported an mZBI score of ≥ 18. Caregivers of cats with IRIS stages 3/4 had significantly higher mZBI scores (median 20.0, range 3 - 50) than caregivers of cats with IRIS stages 1/2 (median 14.5, range 0 - 58; P = 0.0007). Caregivers who reported never to rarely sharing care responsibilities had significantly higher mZBI scores (median 20.0; range 0 - 50) than those who reported sometimes to always sharing care responsibilities (median 15.0; range 2 - 58) (P = 0.0007). Caregivers who reported the need to coax their cat to eat on a daily basis had higher mZBI scores (median 22.8, range 2 - 50) than those who never coaxed their cat to eat (median 14.5, range 0-49) or coaxed their cat 1-2 days/week (median 19.2, range 3 - 42) (both P < 0.001). Caregivers who always felt supported by the veterinary care team had lower mZBI scores (median 13; range 0-58) than those that only felt supported sometimes to never (median 23; range 5-45) (P < 0.001).Conclusions and clinical importanceSignificant caregiver burden is present in feline CKD, emphasizing the need to for clinicians to provide empathetic advice and practical support.

papers.title: Candida albicans Urinary Tract Infection with Suspected Fungal Hepatobiliary Disease in an Immunosuppressed Dog: A Case Report.
papers.authors: Norman A, Walton-Clark M
papers.abstract: Fungal urinary tract infections (UTIs) are uncommon in dogs and are typically associated with immunocompromised patients or those with other predisposing factors. Fungal hepatobiliary disease is rarely reported in the veterinary literature. This case report describes a dog on dual immunosuppressive therapy for suspected immune-mediated polyarthritis that developed a hepatopathy suspected to represent bacterial hepatobiliary disease and was subsequently treated with prolonged amoxicillin-clavulanate therapy. Following treatment, the dog developed marked hepatocellular enzyme elevations together with a Candida albicans UTI. Given the patient's progressive hepatocellular injury, clinical signs, history of immunosuppression and antibiotic therapy, concurrent fungal hepatobiliary involvement was suspected. Following initiation of oral fluconazole, the fungal UTI resolved, and there was marked improvement, with subsequent normalisation of ALT and ALP activities. Although the temporal association between antifungal treatment and clinical and biochemical improvement raised suspicion of concurrent fungal hepatobiliary involvement, simultaneous discontinuation of amoxicillin-clavulanate, substantial reduction in prednisolone dose, and continuation of hepatoprotective therapy precluded attribution of the improvement specifically to antifungal treatment. This case highlights the potential for opportunistic fungal disease in immunosuppressed dogs, particularly following prolonged antimicrobial exposure, and illustrates the diagnostic challenges associated with suspected hepatobiliary involvement.

papers.title: The canine tumour micro-environment and advances in antitumour therapy in canine melanoma.
papers.authors: Hindriks E, Zandvliet MMJM, Sijts AJAM, Broere F
papers.abstract: Cancer poses a substantial health burden in both humans and dogs. Despite significant advances, durable tumour control is often not achieved, highlighting the need for novel targeted therapies and immunotherapies. However, translation of these approaches into human and veterinary oncology has been slow. Comparative oncology offers a valuable translational strategy, as naturally occurring cancers in dogs share significant clinical, molecular, and genetic similarities with human malignancies. This review provides an overview of the canine tumour microenvironment (TME), with a primary focus on melanoma as an aggressive and immunogenic tumour model. Key immune components, including T cells, B cells, natural killer cells, tumour-associated macrophages, and myeloid-derived suppressor cells, are discussed in the context of tumour progression and immune evasion. Furthermore, current advances in immunotherapeutic strategies, such as immune checkpoint inhibitors and therapeutic cancer vaccines, as well as receptor tyrosine kinase-targeted therapies, are evaluated in canine cancers. While these approaches have shown promise, challenges such as tumour heterogeneity, immunosuppressive TMEs, and therapeutic resistance are difficult to overcome, resulting in limited clinical efficacy. Integrating insights from human and veterinary oncology underscores the potential of comparative approaches to improve translational success and develop more effective combination therapies for both species.

papers.title: Procedural sedation with subcutaneously administered medetomidine-vatinoxan-butorphanol in dogs - A randomized, controlled, clinical dose-finding study.
papers.authors: Honkavaara J, Lindh E, Turunen H, Mäki T, Välimäki E, Reunanen V, Vartia N
papers.abstract: Subcutaneous (SC) drug administration may be better tolerated when compared with the intramuscular (IM) route in some dogs. This study investigated the dose-response to subcutaneously administered medetomidine-vatinoxan-butorphanol in producing sedation for orthopedic radiography. Fifty-three privately-owned, healthy dogs were randomly allocated to receive IM medetomidine 0.6 mg/m2 (M0.6-IM), IM medetomidine/vatinoxan 0.6/12 mg/m2 (Z0.6-IM), SC medetomidine/vatinoxan 0.6/12 (Z0.6-SC), 0.9/18 (Z0.9-SC) or 1.2/24 mg/m2 (Z1.2-SC). All treatments included 0.2 mg/kg of butorphanol. Sedation onset and rescue sedation for radiography were recorded. Mean arterial pressures (MAP) and heart rates (HR) were measured and oral mucosal microcirculation quantified with Laser Doppler Flow (LDF) and tissue hemoglobin saturation percentage (T-HbO2). Compared with the SC groups, sedation occurred earlier after both IM treatments. Rescue sedation was administered for 4/11 (Z0.6-SC), 2/10 (Z0.9-SC), 1/10 (Z1.2-SC), 0/11 (Z0.6-IM) and 1/11 dogs (M0.6-IM), respectively. HR decreased significantly from baseline after all treatments while hypotension (MAP < 60 mmHg) was not observed. After M0.6-IM, median (range) LDF 55 (36 - 113) perfusion units (PU) and T-HbO2 64 (49 - 79) % were significantly lower than after Z0.6-IM: 155 (105 - 312) PU and 81 (67 - 87) %; Z0.9-SC: 196 (126 - 492) PU and 79 (72-94) %; Z0.9-SC: 163 (68 - 465) PU and 77 (72 - 84) % and Z1.2-SC: 146 (82 - 422) PU and 77 (69 - 85) %, with no significant differences between the vatinoxan-treatments. Subcutaneously administered medetomidine-vatinoxan-butorphanol appeared efficacious albeit less potent than the IM route in producing sedation in healthy dogs. The hemodynamic improvement by vatinoxan extended to SC co-administration with medetomidine-butorphanol.

papers.title: Cat Stress Score and hair cortisol concentrations are not associated with subclinical hypertrophic cardiomyopathy in cats.
papers.authors: Seo J, Williams M, Munday JS, Connolly DJ, Hunt H
papers.abstract: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) is a common heart disease in domestic cats, but most lack an identifiable cause. This prospective case-control study tested the hypothesis that chronic stress predisposes cats to HCM. Ten cats with echocardiographically confirmed subclinical HCM were compared with 10 healthy cats, HCM-negative cats matched for husbandry, age, sex, and neuter status. Stress was assessed via visual Cat-Stress-Score and hair cortisol concentrations, measured using an enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay from full-length hair samples collected from the lumbar region. Cat-Stress-Scores did not differ between groups across four time points (median 23.3 in the HCM group [range: 17.8-34.0] versus median 25.5 in the control group [range: 21.8-29.2], P = 0.241). Likewise, hair cortisol concentrations did not differ between groups (median 0.25 ng/mL [range: 0.15-0.35] in the HCM group and median 0.19 ng/mL [range: 0.09-0.29] in the control group, P = 0.267). In conclusion, cats with pre-existing subclinical HCM did not display greater stress than healthy controls on the measures of stress assessed.

papers.title: MRI findings in cauda equina nerve roots and associated clinical signs in dogs with degenerative lumbosacral stenosis.
papers.authors: Siauciunaite A, Alder D, Richter H, Steffen F
papers.abstract: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is the most commonly used advanced imaging modality for diagnosing degenerative lumbosacral stenosis (DLSS). However, stenosis of the central canal and intervertebral foramina does not reliably correlate with clinical signs, and additional diagnostic imaging criteria would strengthen the validity of MRI. This study aimed to evaluate the size, signal characteristics, position (nerve root sedimentation sign, NRSS), and course (redundant nerve roots, RNR) of cauda equina nerve roots in dogs with and without DLSS using high-field MRI, and to assess associations between these findings and clinical signs. A retrospective, blinded, case-control study was performed in client-owned dogs, including 50 dogs diagnosed with DLSS and 17 control dogs without clinical signs of DLSS. Lumbosacral foraminal stenosis was identified in 33/50 (66%) DLSS cases and 1/17 (5.88%) controls (p < 0.001, φ = 0.56). Lumbar nerve root pathology was observed in 30/50 (60%) cases and 2/17 (11.77%) controls (p < 0.001, φ = 0.42). A significant association was found between unilateral clinical signs and ipsilateral foraminal stenosis (p = 0.014, φ = 0.40 for the left; p = 0.018, φ = 0.43 for the right side). Ipsilateral thickening of the L7 nerve root was also significantly associated with unilateral nerve root dysfunction (p = 0.033, φ = 0.35 for the left; p = 0.01, φ = 0.45 for the right side). The NRSS findings did not differ significantly between case and control dogs (p = 0.237, φ = 0.15), whereas RNR showed a small to moderate association with DLSS (p < 0.028, φ = 0.27). While NRSS and RNR were not clearly associated with clinical signs in dogs with DLSS, thickening of the L7 nerve root showed significant correlation with clinical dysfunction. The presence of increased nerve root size may enhance the diagnostic utility of high-field MRI in dogs with DLSS.

papers.title: Clinical outcomes were evaluated in 82 dogs with B-cell lymphoma treated with adoptive T-cell therapy following cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin, vincristine, and prednisone chemotherapy.
papers.authors: Westfall TE, Impellizeri JA
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To describe clinical outcomes and adverse events in dogs with B-cell lymphoma treated with adoptive T-cell therapy (ACT) following cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin, vincristine, and prednisone (CHOP) chemotherapy. METHODS: Medical records of 82 dogs with B-cell lymphoma that received ACT following CHOP chemotherapy between 2017 and 2025 were retrospectively reviewed. Overall survival was defined as the time from lymphoma diagnosis to death from any cause or last follow-up. Post-ACT survival was defined as the time from first ACT infusion to death from any cause or last follow-up. Time to next anti-lymphoma treatment was defined as the time from first ACT infusion to initiation of subsequent lymphoma-directed therapy. Survival outcomes were estimated using Kaplan-Meier analysis. RESULTS: 82 dogs met inclusion criteria. Median overall survival from diagnosis was 660 days (95% CI, 539 to 781 days). Median post-ACT survival was 368 days (95% CI, 261 to 474 days), and median time to next anti-lymphoma treatment was 317 days (95% CI, 284 to 350 days). Adoptive T-cell therapy was generally well tolerated following CHOP chemotherapy. Adverse events occurred in 5% (4 of 82) of dogs; most were grade 1 or 2, with 1 grade 3 event reported. CONCLUSIONS: Clinical outcomes varied among dogs with B-cell lymphoma treated with ACT following CHOP chemotherapy. Adoptive T-cell therapy was generally well tolerated, with adverse events reported in 4 of 82 dogs. CLINICAL RELEVANCE: This study describes clinical outcomes and adverse events in 82 dogs with B-cell lymphoma that received ACT following CHOP chemotherapy. These findings provide clinical data on the use of ACT in this patient population and may inform the design of prospective controlled studies evaluating ACT in canine B-cell lymphoma.
